desc:
grid has exactly two rows and n columns. You may choose any set of cells, but no two chosen cells may share a side (cells that only touch at a corner are fine). Return the largest possible sum of the chosen values. Choosing nothing is allowed, so the answer is never negative.

For example, in [[3, 1, 4], [2, 7, 1]] choose the top cell of column 0, the bottom cell of column 1 and the top cell of column 2: 3 + 7 + 4 = 14.
hints: In any single column you can choose nothing, only the top cell or only the bottom cell, but never both. That is three states per column.
Which choice in column c-1 is compatible with 'top' in column c? Not 'top', but 'nothing' and 'bottom' are fine, and symmetrically for 'bottom'.
Keep three running values for the previous column: best with nothing chosen, with the top cell chosen, with the bottom cell chosen. Update them column by column.
editorial: Process columns left to right and keep none, top, bottom: the best sum so far when the current column has no chosen cell, only its top cell, or only its bottom cell. For the next column with values a (top) and b (bottom): none' = max(none, top, bottom), top' = a + max(none, bottom) and bottom' = b + max(none, top).

A choice only conflicts with the same row of the previous column or the other cell of its own column, which the transitions exclude. The answer is the maximum of the three after the last column, starting from none = 0 and the other two impossible. Time O(n), space O(1). This is House Robber lifted from a path to a 2 x n ladder graph.
